name: Continental Baroque & Neoclassical

description.short: The French-led sequence from Baroque grandeur through Neoclassical restraint to the Beaux-Arts system that trained a generation of American architects.
description.long:
France took the Italian classical inheritance and made it a state apparatus: an academy, a curriculum, a hierarchy of building types, and a method of composition taught by competition. The Baroque phase pursued theatrical spatial effect; the Neoclassical reaction pursued archaeological correctness and structural honesty; the Beaux-Arts synthesis systematized both into a teachable design process built on parti, poché, and axial hierarchy.

For American residential architecture this family matters chiefly through the Ecole des Beaux-Arts, where Richardson, Hunt, and hundreds of others trained. The eclectic revivals of 1880–1940 are not naive antiquarianism; they are the product of a rigorous compositional education applied to borrowed vocabularies.

defining_characteristics: Composition taught as a formal discipline: parti, axis, hierarchy, poché
State and academy as patrons and standard-setters
Archaeological correctness as a competing value against expressive effect
